findings.finding: Received body and tx durability completion no longer forks linked Async continuations. processLeiosBlock synchronously awaits point then body writes, and only afterward inserts body cache/claims acquired state/credits fresh bytes; ingestAcquiredTxs synchronously awaits writeTxs before onDurable request completion and cache/location updates. DB waits are outside the outstandingVar critical section. No local mask/restore wrapper is added; ambient masking is inherited.
findings.impact: Actual protocol collector may now remain blocked on DB durability and may receive cancellation or errors there. The prior separate linked completion-worker lifetime is removed at these sites, but physical worker exit/DB-job completion/CM result publication remain separate facts.

findings.finding: BodyImminent and markBodyImminent are removed. ForgedLocally announcement does not register fetch work; after durable body write acquireForgedEbBody installs BodyAcquired empty job pool even if a peer copy had pending jobs.
findings.impact: Different legal body-fetch/state transitions; prevents the modeled source self-fetch window described by the patch, but no universal end-to-end proof or replay was run.

findings.finding: LeiosTxCache.insertBody loses caller accumulator/location lookup; separate lookupTxLocations read obtains fill sources before the write, and insertBody occurs after the write. Optimized backend uses withMVar for location lookup and modifyMVar for insert; stale locations remain guarded by DB fill logic.
findings.impact: Cache possession follows durability rather than preceding it; app wait/state/error schedules change. Exact callback/storage correspondence must reflect this order.

findings.finding: SQLite LeiosDB API/writer/queue/Completion sources are byte-identical241→current. Promise wraps await; submitJob atomically enqueues then returns a Promise waiting on resultTMVar or queue seal. That await has no removal/cancel-job operation. startWriter runs in node ResourceRegistry and seals/rethrows failures.
findings.impact: Inference: after successful submission, cancellation of the awaiting protocol worker alone does not remove its queued DB job; independent writer work may continue. Synchronous callbacks do not establish whole-node/API quiescence or change CM ownership.
